topic: Specification of hydraulic oil, need for clean pipelines and use of protective ointment while handling oils.
syllabus_extract: Specification of hydraulic oil, need for clean pipelines and use of protective ointment while handling oils.
specific_objectives: 17.1.2.1 Trainee will be able to describe typical hydraulic system and construction of its components.

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Demonstration of oil spill containment and application of protective ointment on skin; Safety: Wear gloves and eye protection; Supervision: Instructor monitors technique and safety compliance.
intro_questions: What is the primary function of hydraulic fluid in an aircraft system?
Why must hydraulic pipelines be free from contaminants before installation?
What type of injury can occur from direct contact with hydraulic oil?

topics: Flash point and fire hazard limits
development.content:
Viscosity and temperature characteristics
Flash point and fire hazard limits
Anti-corrosion and anti-wear additives
Compatibility with seals and hoses
Standard specification grades for aircraft

topics: Impact of particulates on valve operation
Procedures for cleaning pipelines during maintenance
development.content:

Impact of particulates on valve operation
Water contamination and freezing risks

topics: Purpose of protective ointment on skin
Storage and disposal of used ointment
development.content:

Removal procedures after handling
Storage and disposal of used ointment
Safety precautions during ointment application

summary_questions: Explain why hydraulic oil specifications vary between different aircraft systems.
Describe the consequences of using oil with incorrect viscosity in a hydraulic system.
List three reasons why clean pipelines are critical for hydraulic system reliability.
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief report comparing the properties of hydraulic oil used in LP 02 versus current system requirements, highlighting differences in specification.
